gate: C9 projectable HMT U(1) quantum-evaluability preflight
question: Are the currently source-locked projectable HMT U(1) gravitational inputs sufficient to define a unique gauge-fixed quadratic one-loop problem (Hessian plus ghost/constraint measure) without importing the ordinary-projectable parent quantization or inventing a new gauge prescription?
required_quantum_inputs: one explicit projectable HMT U(1) gravitational action with A and Newtonian prepotential nu
complete gauge transformations for the fields retained in the quantum calculation
explicit gauge-fixing functional for foliation-preserving diffeomorphisms and local U(1)
corresponding Faddeev-Popov/BRST ghost operator or equivalent reduced-measure prescription
treatment of first-/second-class constraints sufficient to define the functional determinant
background about which the quadratic Hessian is taken
decision_rule: PASS_SCOPED means the existing source lock is enough to identify the classical projectable HMT U(1) constrained field content, but not enough to define a unique one-loop functional determinant because an HMT-specific gauge-fixing/ghost-or-BRST prescription is not source-locked. This is an evaluability blocker, not a claim of nonrenormalizability.
nonclaims: No literature-wide claim that no HMT U(1) BRST formulation exists.
No claim that projectable HMT U(1) gravity is nonrenormalizable.
No beta functions are assigned to A, nu, or the unresolved matter interface.
No closure of full C9 radiative naturalness.
No soft-s retest or k=0.03 production is enabled.
